messages:
ciara: did a quick multi-region smoke run for L4 / T4 / A10G — embeddings + small-chat (2-turn). uploading raw CSVs and a tiny summary here.
sam: awesome. which regions?
ciara: us-west1, us-east1, eu-central1. workloads: embeddings (batch=64,256) and small-chat (batch=8, max_tokens=128). quant profiles: fp16 baseline, q4_0 and int8-dynamic on compatible builds.
mike: any surprises on kernels? did you test cutlass vs triton vs our lightweight fused kernels?
ciara: yes — short notes:
- A10G: flash-attn + cutlass path gave best latency for chat (p50 ~ 6–9ms/token for 2-turns, p95 ~ 12–18ms/token). embeddings throughput highest on A10G with batch=256.
- T4: triton path was okay for embeddings but p95 for chat was 1.6–2× higher than A10G at same batch. int8 reduced memory but added ~10% latency on T4.
- L4: our open kernels (kernel-v2) had lower peak throughput but consistent tail latencies; good cost point for embeddings at medium batch sizes.
anya: cost numbers? rough $/1M tokens?
ciara: rough ballpark from the run (region=us-west1): A10G fp16 chat ~ $12 / 1M tokens (high throughput, low latency). T4 fp16 chat ~ $7 / 1M tokens but with higher p95. L4 fp16 embeddings (batch=256) ~ $2.5 / 1M tokens (cheap for embedding-heavy workloads). quantized q4_0 reduces cost by ~20–30% on A10G/T4 for embeddings with small quality hit.
perf-bot: summary generated -> https://internal-reports/redwood/bench/1765123456 (csv + pngs). :white_check_mark:
sam: did you compare kernel memory footprints? we need to know allowed KV cache sizing for 8-token lookups.
ciara: yes — flash-attn + cutlass used ~30% more vram than triton on same batch but drastically lower compute time. L4 kernel-v2 had smallest footprint but needed tighter batching to hit throughput.
mike: any quality regressions with q4_0 on small-chat?
ciara: minor regression in rare cases (repetition on short prompts). we flagged with eval-set A (10k prompts). recommend using q4_0 only for embeddings/low-criticality chat or pairing with safety fallback to fp16 for canary traffic.
anya: next steps?
ciara: 1) run longer-run stability test (24h) on T4 and L4 in eu-central1, 2) add kernel fallback policy in routing (prefer A10G for low-latency chat), 3) push quantized eval alerts to Redwood Optimize.
sam: thanks — can you drop the CSVs in the eng-ml drive and tag infra to reserve 2x A10G for the 24h? :thumbsup:
ciara: yup, done. link in perf-bot summary above.
